legal_basis: Constitution of Kenya 2010, Chapter 10 (Articles 162-169); Judicature Act; Magistrates' Courts Act

hierarchy.name: Supreme Court
hierarchy.composition: Chief Justice (President), Deputy Chief Justice (Deputy President), and 5 other judges (7 total); quorum of 5
hierarchy.jurisdiction: Exclusive original jurisdiction over presidential election petitions; appellate jurisdiction over Court of Appeal decisions on matters of constitutional interpretation or certified as of general public importance; final and binding, subject to its own limited review power

hierarchy.name: Court of Appeal
hierarchy.jurisdiction: Hears appeals from the High Court and courts of equal status (Employment and Labour Relations Court, Environment and Land Court)
hierarchy.appeals_to: Supreme Court (on constitutional interpretation or matters of general public importance)

hierarchy.name: High Court
hierarchy.jurisdiction: Unlimited original jurisdiction in criminal and civil matters; supervisory jurisdiction over subordinate courts and tribunals; hears constitutional petitions and judicial review applications; hears appeals from Magistrates' Courts and tribunals

hierarchy.name: Employment and Labour Relations Court
hierarchy.jurisdiction: Employment and labour relations disputes; status equal to the High Court

hierarchy.name: Environment and Land Court
hierarchy.jurisdiction: Environment, and use, occupation and title to land disputes; status equal to the High Court

hierarchy.name: Magistrates' Courts
hierarchy.jurisdiction: Bulk of criminal and civil trials at first instance, within pecuniary/penal limits set by rank

hierarchy.name: Kadhis' Courts
hierarchy.jurisdiction: Questions of Muslim personal law relating to marriage, divorce, inheritance, where all parties profess the Muslim faith and submit to the court's jurisdiction

hierarchy.name: Courts Martial
hierarchy.jurisdiction: Service offences committed by members of the Kenya Defence Forces

hierarchy.name: Small Claims Court
hierarchy.constitutional_basis: Article 169; Small Claims Court Act, 2016 (operational from 2021)
hierarchy.jurisdiction: Civil claims for a liquidated sum or value of subject matter not exceeding the statutory limit (KES 1,000,000 as of last update); simplified, expeditious procedure; no legal representation as of right at first instance

hierarchy.name: Other Tribunals
hierarchy.constitutional_basis: Article 169; various enabling Acts of Parliament
hierarchy.jurisdiction: Specialised, sector-specific disputes (e.g. Rent Restriction Tribunal, Business Premises Rent Tribunal, Tax Appeals Tribunal, Political Parties Disputes Tribunal, Public Procurement Administrative Review Board, Cooperative Tribunal); no penal jurisdiction; generally operate under High Court supervision
hierarchy.appeals_to: High Court (or as specified in the tribunal's enabling Act)

notes: Superior courts (tiers 1-3) are the Supreme Court, Court of Appeal, High Court, Employment and Labour Relations Court, and Environment and Land Court.
Subordinate courts (tier 4) are Magistrates' Courts, Kadhis' Courts, Courts Martial, the Small Claims Court, and other tribunals established by Act of Parliament.

General appeal timelines: 30 days from Magistrates' Court to High Court (civil); 14 days (criminal); 30 days from High Court to Court of Appeal; 30 days from Court of Appeal to Supreme Court on constitutional matters.

This reflects the structure as generally described by the Judiciary of Kenya and the Constitution; specific monetary/jurisdictional thresholds for Magistrates' Courts and the Small Claims Court are set by subsidiary legislation and are periodically revised — verify current thresholds against the Judiciary's own publications before relying on them for filing decisions.
